chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from al-Mukhtar ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abdullah ibn al-Husayn, all of them, from al-Fath ibn Yazid, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the conditions in Mut'ah (temporary marriage). He said: The conditions in it are such and such. If she says 'Yes', then that is permissible. And I do not say as was reported to me that the people of Iraq say: 'The water is yours and the land is yours, and I do not water your land with the water, and if something grows there, it belongs to the owner of the land,' because two conditions in one condition is invalid. And if you are granted a child, you accept it. And the matter is clear. So whoever wishes to confuse himself, let him confuse himself.

key_terms.أَهْلَ الْعِرَاقِ: The people of Iraq (a specific juristic school or group)

ai.seo_question: What are the valid conditions in temporary marriage according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) refutes the Iraqi juristic contention that a husband can conditionally withhold water rights to the land, thereby invalidating the produce, by identifying it as a 'condition within a condition' (shartan fi shart) which renders the stipulation void. This ruling underscores the flexibility of Mut'ah contracts in Shia jurisprudence, affirming that unless explicitly agreed upon, such specific property rights do not automatically transfer or restrict the marriage's validity, ensuring the legitimacy of offspring remains unchallenged.
